newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Salomon sees Europe's car sales up, trucks down.
newsitem.headline: Salomon sees Europe's car sales up, trucks down.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said on Wednesday it saw the Western European market for cars growing 2.9 percent this year, while it forecast that heavy trucks sales will fall between six and seven percent in 1997.
"We continue to expect a stronger (car) market based on two positives," Salomon Brothers analyst John Lawson said in an analysis called European Auto Digest.
"First, the underlying economics -- notwithstanding continued fiscal stringency -- are widely forecast to be better. Salomon expects a trend 2.4 percent growth rate in Europe this year."
"Second, accelerated replacement demand should continue to be a very active feature of the car market."
He said the Western European car market would grow 2.9 percent this year and 3.5 percent next year.
In 1997, he saw the Italian market as the top performer, up 14 percent fuelled by government incentives, while he expected the French market to fall by 8.1 percent.
But Salomon Brothers expected heavy truck sales in Western Europe to fall between six and seven percent, before recovering to grow one percent next year.

"With the poor exit rate from 1996, new truck registrations are highly likely to show poor performance in early 1997 and we expect to see double-digit declines in sales in the early part of the year," Lawson said.
But he said sales would stabilise later during the year, falling between six and seven percent year-on-year during 1997.
He expected the French and Italian markets to be the weakest, while he saw the Dutch and British markets as the strongest.
Total Western Europe heavy truck sales were expected to be 160,300 vehicles in 1997, compared with 171,747 in 1996, while 1998 will see sales of 161,900 units, he said.
